messages:
maria: Quick question for the group — we need a decision on how SLO-driven routing should pick between regional fallback (route to another region) vs model-variant fallback (downgrade to a cheaper/quantized model) for paid tiers. Also need an ops-facing console control for circuit-breaker thresholds per tier.

oliver: Are we talking about two independent fallback axes (region and model) with a priority order, or a single policy that chooses based on cost/latency estimates?

tanya: From UX side, we should let teams express a preference list (primary: same region+primary model, fallback1: same region+quantized model, fallback2: other region+primary model). But expose an override toggle: "prefer local" vs "prefer model parity".

raj: For CB thresholds we need concrete signals. Proposal: p95 latency > X ms for Y consecutive windows OR error rate > Z% => trip. We should tie X,Y,Z to tier defaults but allow per-customer overrides.

maria: nailed it. Example defaults by tier? free: p95=1000ms, errors=5%, pro: p95=400ms, errors=1%, enterprise: p95=200ms, errors=0.5% (but negotiable). Thoughts?

stan: We also need telemetry names and tags so billing/alerts map cleanly: e.g., metric: rrt.p95_ms, tag:tier=pro, tag:fallback=region/model/none, tag:model_variant=redwood-7b-q4f. That allows us to query how often model fallback was used.

oliver: Implementation note: runtime needs a small policy object on each request to evaluate. Something like: 
```json
{
  "tier": "pro",
  "latency_slo_ms": 400,
  "circuit_breaker": {"p95_threshold_ms": 650, "window_seconds": 60, "consecutive_windows": 2, "error_rate_pct": 1.0},
  "fallback_order": ["model_variant_local", "region_primary"],
  "fallback_policy": {"model_variant_local": {"variant": "q4f"}}
}
```
This would let runtime evaluate quickly.

tanya: For Console: show an interactive preview that simulates routing decisions given current telemetry. Ops can tweak p95 threshold sliders and see projected fallback % and cost delta. Very important to have a "simulate with sample traffic" button.

raj: Also add an API to run a dry-run rollout: POST /policy/simulate with a time range and get back counts of requests that would have fallen back to each path. We should gate real changes behind a successful simulation or incremental canary.

maria: Agree on dry-run. Also need to document rollback behaviour: if CB trips, should we auto-untrip after N windows below threshold or require manual ack for enterprise? Suggest default auto-untrip after 10 windows below threshold, enterprise has optional manual.

stan: Telemetry hooks: emit event on every decision: decision.fallback.chosen (fields: request_id, tier, chosen, reason: latency|errors|capacity, prior_model, chosen_model, src_region, dst_region). That makes postmortems trivial.

oliver: Small API debate: should policy be nested under customer config or live in a global policy service? I vote customer config with global defaults that can be overridden — simpler for per-customer rollouts and billing.

tanya: UX caveat: if policies are per-customer we need a concise diff view in Console for changes (what changed vs default) and a one-click revert. Keep the default UI simple for small teams.

raj: Ops alerting: different severity for tiers. When enterprise tier trips, page oncall (P1). When free trips, create ticket but don't page. We should encode that mapping into the policy metadata.

deploy-bot: Simulation job 2002467890-sim-1 completed: projected fallback rate=3.7%, cost delta +9% if prefer model parity. Link: https://ci.internal/sim/2002467890-sim-1

maria: Nice — @tanya can you prototype the Console mock and @oliver can you draft the policy JSON shape and API endpoints? I'll draft the default thresholds and a short runbook for CB trips.

tanya: On it, will push a few mock images to Figma and share.

oliver: I'll open an RFC with example telemetry queries and the API surface: POST /policies/:customer_id, GET /policies/:customer_id/simulate. Will include sample rollout strategy (canary percent, dry-run duration).

raj: I'll wire up alert rules and make sure we have dashboards: one for fallback rates by tier, one for CB state by region, one for decision latency.

maria: Thanks all. Last ask: add a short one-paragraph blurb for support docs so CS can explain what "model fallback" means to customers.

stan: I'll add glossary entries and sample queries.

maria: Cool, will sync at the weekly infra sync. :thumbsup:
